mutation_targets.rationale: removing this fact lets the model invent a successful DeleteTask by a same-team member who is not the owner and not a sharee — exactly the permission-bypass LeastPrivilege guards against. With the matrix only granting DeleteTask to OwnerRel and AdminRel, an InTeamNoneRel success is a counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilegeViolation { some op: Operation | op.successful = BTrue and op.kind = DeleteTask and one op.target and op.caller != op.target.owner and op.caller.role = Member and op.caller not in op.target.sharedWith and op.caller.team = op.target.taskTeam and op.authenticated = BTrue }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing this fact lets two distinct operations share a single AuditEntry, which is the structural shape of an entry being re-used or rewritten — the exact thing the FR-017 append-only invariant forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj op1, op2: Operation, ae: AuditEntry | ae in op1.producedAudit and ae in op2.producedAudit }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing this fact lets a successful mutation exist with no audit entry, which is the missing-audit failure mode FR-015 and AuditCompleteness are meant to catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCompletenessViolation { some op: Operation | op.successful = BTrue and op.kind = PatchTaskFields and one op.target and op.caller = op.target.owner and op.authenticated = BTrue and no op.producedAudit }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing this fact lets the model invent a successful operation with no authentication — the precise scenario AuthRequiredEverywhere is designed to forbid (FR-001 401-before-business-logic).
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuthRequiredViolation { some op: Operation | op.successful = BTrue and op.authenticated = BFalse and op.kind = GetTask }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing this fact lets an audit entry record an actor different from the operation's actual caller — the misattribution AttributionCorrectness guards against (FR-016 actor/role snapshot fidelity).
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AttributionViolation { some op: Operation, ae: AuditEntry | ae in op.producedAudit and ae.actor != op.caller }

mutation_targets.rationale: removing this fact lets a task be shared with a user outside the owner's team, the cross-team sharing leak FR-012 explicitly forbids and which would break the FR-014 byte-equivalence invariant through the sharing path.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CrossTeamShareViolation { some t: Task, u: t.sharedWith | u.team != t.taskTeam }
